findings.finding: Conversation lookup in POST /roommate-profiles/:id/message uses participants.every(userId in [a,b]) to find an existing 1:1 conversation, which is only correct because conversations are always created with exactly 2 participants. If that invariant is ever broken elsewhere, this could theoretically misidentify a conversation.
findings.recommendedAction: Non-blocking defense-in-depth improvement: match on participant count === 2 as well, or query by exact participant set. Not required for this MVP.

findings.finding: Backend correctness (tsc, prisma generate/validate, migration generation) has not been run in this sandbox by any agent, including this review.
findings.recommendedAction: Before merge/deploy, run npm install && npx tsc --noEmit and npx prisma generate/migrate in both rentals/backend and rentals/frontend, per the integrator's own flagged gap. This is a build-verification gap, not a security defect, and does not block security approval.

notes: Reviewed the integrated worktree directly (not prior summaries): rentals/backend/src/routes/roommateProfiles.ts, prisma/schema.prisma (RoommateProfile, Conversation, Report models/enums), admin.ts and messages.ts integration points, socketServer.ts room-join verification, and the frontend api.ts/RoommateProfileDetail.tsx. All create/update/deactivate/reactivate mutations are scoped exclusively to req.user.id via where:{userId:...} with no route accepting a client-supplied id for these operations — IDOR is structurally impossible, not just checked. PUBLIC_SELECT is the single, consistently-reused select across browse/detail/me and never includes email/phone/address/lat-lng/contact fields. Detail route returns 404 (not 403) for inactive profiles to non-owners, avoiding existence-confirmation leaks. Entire router requires authentication, meaningfully raising the bar against anonymous scraping of a directory of real people. Zod .strict() schemas bound every field (bio ≤1000, headline 5-200, lifestyleTags from a fixed enum vocabulary only — no free-text discriminatory filter fields), UUIDs validated via validateUuidParam, writeRateLimiter applied to all mutating routes. Reporting reuses the existing Report model/pattern exactly, with admin's existing role-gated (ADMIN|MODERATOR) /admin/reports endpoint extended safely. Frontend renders all profile text (bio, headline) as plain React children — no dangerouslySetInnerHTML anywhere — so no XSS vector. Socket.IO conversation-room joins remain DB-verified generically (not conversation-type-specific), so roommate-profile conversations inherit the same server-side membership check as listing conversations. No findings rise above informational; no CHANGES_REQUIRED items.</notes>
